maria-cs: Heads-up 3 AsterField Medical just submitted an intake. They want a bilingual (EN/ES) discharge summarizer and strict PHI handling. Asking for timeline + safety/regression plan. Paste of their note: 

AsterField Medical (customer):
> We need a discharge summary service for English + Spanish notes. Requirements:
> - PHI must never transit Redwood hosted endpoints; PHI-tagged payloads must route to our Private VPC deployment.
> - Tokenizer must treat IDs (SSN, MRN) and patient names as atomic tokens to avoid redaction errors.
> - Embeddings for search must strip PHI prior to storage; we want an option to store non-PHI embeddings in hosted, but PHI embeddings must be disabled.
> - Offline safety/regression: 75k tokens overall, with A/B comparison to our legacy summarizer.
> - Canary deploy with automatic rollback if p95 latency > 500ms or if regression metrics drop > 5%
> Samples: 3k notes + mapping CSV attached. Target pilot in 4 weeks.

lina-se: routing note: detecting PHI via edge classifier + regex is doable. we'll need a lightweight tagger in the hosted edge to flip the "phi:true" flag to the control plane and then forward to Private. requires their network config for control-plane callbacks.

sam-ml: tokenizer + bilingual support: options:
- build joint tokenizer with special tokens for name/ID spans (recommended). requires regenerating tokenizer vocab and a quick conversion step for model weights.
- run a 2-stage preprocess that canonicalizes names/ids to single tokens, then postmap back (faster, but more brittle).

sam-ml: safety/regressions: 75k tokens is heavier than usual. estimate: 
- smoke eval (5k) in 2 business days
- full 75k harness + analysis ~8 business days (compute + human review for Spanish edge cases)

jessie-sec: security checklist items:
- verify PHI detection rules for Spanish name variants and diacritics
- KMS/HSM for Private keys and audit export to their SIEM
- ensure embedding pipeline has a PHI filter that prevents accidental persistence; disable EH cache for PHI-tagged sessions

andre-cs: i'll schedule kickoff. i'll ask for their VPC/VPN details, SIEM endpoint info, and the legacy summarizer outputs for A/B by EOD tomorrow.

maria-cs: flag for enablement: we should prepare both an EN/ES quickstart and a runbook for their SREs about routing/fallbacks. i'll draft.

lina-se: small config snippet for initial routing rule (for eng):
```yaml
routing_rules:
  - name: phi_span_v2
    match: "regex:\b(SSN|MRN|NPI|patient_name)\b|lang:es"
    action: route_private
fallback_policy:
  latency_threshold_ms: 500
  rollback_on_regression_pct: 5
  fallback_model: small-8b-quant
```

sam-ml: bilingual tokenizer note: watch out for accented characters causing token splits (e.g., Jose9 -> Jo s e9). we'll include normalization rules in the tokenizer build.

jessie-sec: request for legal: we'll prepare a short data-flow diagram and MSA addendum for PHI handling.

onboard-bot: Created onboarding card REDW-5112 -> AsterField bilingual PHI routing. Owner: andre-cs. Due: 1993300000.

andre-cs: action items:
- andre-cs: kickoff call + request network details and legacy outputs (ETA 1 business day)
- sam-ml: begin tokenizer prototype using sample CSV (ETA 4 business days)
- lina-se: open infra ticket for control-plane callbacks + network allowlist (ETA 1 business day)
- jessie-sec: prepare PHI checklist focused on bilingual edge cases (ETA 2 business days)

maria-cs: set expectation with customer: pilot ~4 weeks if artifacts arrive quickly; otherwise +1 week. i'll send the recap to their contact.

sam-ml: note 3 add a validation job post-tokenizer conversion to compare embeddings/logit shifts vs baseline. low-scale job first.

lina-se: i'll coordinate canary schedule with infra and blocking windows.

jessie-sec: will coordinate Legal + Compliance outreach.

maria-cs: closing thread for now. next update after kickoff call. :white_check_mark:
